Subject: Temporary cross-region processing under our DPA — clarification needed

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question as we finish procurement: our legal team wants to confirm what triggers a temporary cross-region processing window under Redwood's DPA. Specifically:

- If there is a brief failover to a neighboring region (EU->US) for up to 72 hours, does that require a DPA addendum or just a notice?
- Will subprocessors (analytics/telemetry) be spun up in the failover region, and if so do we get a roster of which sub‑processors may process Acme data during such a window?
- Can Acme request region pinning (EU-only) with an exception workflow for emergency failover, and what are the operational controls/restraints?

We're near closing and this is the last open item for our privacy team. Appreciate anything you can share or an ETA for a formal addendum.

Thanks,
Sara Brown

Acme Health

Vanessa — quick operational notes (ops lead):

- Trigger definition: failover allowed for regional availability events where >50% pod loss in primary region AND mutual failover threshold met for 10 minutes. That's what automations use today. We can document this as an SRE-determined trigger with customer ops notified.
- Window: 72h is our standard hard cap for temporary cross-region processing. After 72h a mandatory escalation to legal & ops for extended authorization.
- Subprocessors: analytics/metrics pipeline (internal) and our logging vendor may accept transient, scoped messages in the failover region. We can provide a roster of which services will be active and an assurance that only hashed/pseudonymized telemetry will be forwarded when the data class is marked sensitive.
- Telemetry mitigation: we can route telemetry to a pseudonymization layer before egress; full PHI payloads will be blocked by default unless customer grants explicit emergency exception (documented in the addendum).
- Audit & notice: we will emit an automatic console event + email to customer ops within 15 minutes of failover and include a signed acknowledgment step for extended windows.

I'll leave the formal language to Neha for legal framing.

— Karthik

Hi Sara — thanks for the patience. Consolidated answers and next steps below (I've attached the draft addendum and the one‑page ops playbook). If this looks good we'll produce a clean DPA addendum for countersignature.

Summary (short):
1) Failover triggers and window: Redwood supports temporary cross-region failover for operational availability events. Trigger = sustained regional pod loss (>50% for >10 minutes) or catastrophic region outage. Standard hard cap is 72 hours; any extension requires sign-off per the addendum.

2) Subprocessors and telemetry: During an authorized failover some telemetry and logging subprocessors may be activated in the failover region. Redwood will provide a temporary, scoped subprocessor roster for the window and will route sensitive classes through a pseudonymization layer by default. Full PHI payloads are blocked unless Acme enables an emergency exception (documented steps in the addendum).

3) Region pinning + exception workflow: You can elect EU-only residency in the DPA. The exception workflow for emergency failover requires: (a) automatic notification to Acme ops + security; (b) SRE lead approval and console acknowledgment; (c) documented scope & duration (72h default); (d) optional telemetry pseudonymization. All of this will be captured in the DPA addendum and the attached playbook.

Attachments included: Redwood_DPA_Addendum_v1.1.pdf (includes temporary-egress clause, subprocessors scope, and emergency exception process)
ops-pin-playbook-draft.md (one-page operational checklist & notification flow)
subprocessor_roster_202605.csv (temporary roster for scoped failover)

Next steps:
- Please review the addendum and playbook. If you want different default windows (e.g., 48h) note that in a reply and we can propose language.
- If Acme legal wants the addendum redlined, loop me in and I'll coordinate Neha (legal) for final language.

If you prefer a quick 20-minute call this afternoon to walk through, I'm available at 16:00 PST.
